hypotheses_not_established: The repeated return-corridor depletion is consistent with checking how the shared navigator handles energy forecasts, terrain changes and queued commands during a low-battery home leg.
Policy target ordering and when it starts the home leg may contribute, but these records cannot isolate learned choice, feasibility forecast, navigator or queue prediction effects.
No conclusion about optimizer failure, overfitting, causal mechanism, or a safe repair follows from these selected post-hoc cases.
limits: Post-hoc diagnosis on two already evaluated maps selected because failures occurred; no statistical generalization or policy selection.

Truth positions are evaluator-only saved replay states rounded to six decimal places. Public telemetry is separately identified and includes sensing noise/delay; hidden truth was not available to the acting controller.
Sampled value zeroed by survival factor describes recorded credited samples before the death penalty, not value a hypothetical repaired trajectory would necessarily bank.
Goal intentions are recorded high-level choices; the inherited controller produces and may override low-level commands. Saved commands do not expose every internal guard estimate.
Existing final evaluation audit is reported by parent; this extractor verifies hashes/identities and reads recorded state, but does not re-simulate or independently re-audit physics.
method: Standard-library inspection of existing JSON/gzip only; no project imports, simulations, tool calls to environment, policy inference, optimization, model API or cloud work.
observations: All three PPO 8192 policies die on world 82001; all three matched-2048 PPO policies, both scripted controls, and all retained replay policies survive and return home on that world.

The PPO 8192 return legs on 82001 end in the same small region east of base, at ticks 362, 364 and 379, with rocks recorded at death. Their final chosen goal suffix is d8, d5, base. PPO17 and PPO29 share the first 15 chosen goals exactly.
PPO29 at 2048 on world 82024 dies at tick 384 just outside the base radius; its 8192 counterpart and both controls survive and return home.

All four failed traces select base before death and retain a feasible direct-home public forecast at that decision. None executes a wait after the final base choice before dying. This is an observed forecast/execution outcome mismatch, not proof of a particular cause.

At fatal command send time the latest received telemetry is three ticks old; the fatal drive executes four ticks after send. This is visible recorded latency, not evidence that latency alone caused the death.
